Counsel,

Please find attached our initial draft of the Executive Employment Agreement for your review. We have proposed a straightforward structure covering the COO role, base compensation and benefits, severance on a qualifying termination, and a limited post-employment non-compete.

We look forward to your comments.

Best,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: PARTIES. This Executive Employment Agreement is entered into by and between Vireo Systems Inc., a Delaware corporation, and the Executive identified on the signature page hereto.
edits.name: Parties

edits.text: 1. POSITION. The Executive shall serve as Chief Operating Officer and shall report to the Chief Executive Officer. The Executive shall devote substantially all business time, attention, skill, and efforts to the performance of the Executive's duties and shall comply with all lawful policies and directions of the Company.
edits.name: Position

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of USD 350,000, payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices, less applicable withholdings and deductions. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the Company's employee benefit plans generally made available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to the terms and conditions of such plans, as amended from time to time.
edits.name: Compensation

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive's employment without Cause, then, subject to the Executive's execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims in favor of the Company and continued compliance with all restrictive covenants, the Executive shall receive severance equal to six months of the Executive's then-current base salary, payable in substantially equal installments in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices.
edits.name: Severance

edits.text: 4. NON-COMPETE. During employment and for twelve months following the termination of employment for any reason, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, provide services to, or hold any material financial interest in any business that competes with the Company in any geographic area in which the Company conducts or has taken material steps to conduct business, except that the Executive may own up to two percent of the outstanding securities of any publicly traded company. This covenant shall apply only to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.
edits.name: Non-Compete

receiver.message_back: Counsel, thank you—our client can proceed with the COO framework if the economics and exit protections are brought in line with market: base salary at $425,000, eligibility for an annual target bonus of 50% of base, equity participation to be separately documented, and severance of 12 months’ base salary plus target bonus and COBRA continuation upon termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason. The 12-month non-compete is not acceptable as drafted; at most we can consider a narrowly tailored 6-month customer/employee non-solicit and confidentiality/IP covenants, subject to applicable law.

drafter.private_reasoning: Opposing counsel has moved materially on the business framework but is asking for a significant economics uplift and deletion of the non-compete. To keep momentum while protecting Vireo, I would counter with an increased base salary and target bonus below their ask, equity only if approved and separately documented, and severance enhanced to 9 months base salary only plus limited COBRA reimbursement. Given enforceability concerns, I would pivot from the broad 12-month non-compete to a more defensible 9-month non-solicit/non-interference package plus confidentiality/IP covenants, preserving maximum enforceability without creating a stalemate over a covenant that may be difficult to enforce.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Thank you for the constructive response. We have revised the draft to reflect a COO package that meaningfully moves toward your client’s proposal while remaining consistent with Vireo’s senior executive compensation structure and current plan design.

In particular, we have increased base salary to $400,000, added eligibility for a 40% annual target bonus, and included a placeholder acknowledging that any equity participation will be separately documented and subject to Board approval and applicable plan terms. We have also enhanced severance to 9 months of base salary, plus up to 9 months of COBRA premium reimbursement, subject to the customary release and continuing covenant compliance.

On restrictive covenants, in light of your comments, we have removed the broad 12-month non-compete concept and replaced it with a more tailored 9-month customer and employee non-solicit/non-interference covenant, together with confidentiality and IP protections to be included in the final agreement and ancillary documents. We believe this is a reasonable and enforceable middle ground that addresses Vireo’s legitimate business interests without overreaching.

Please let us know if your client can proceed on this basis so we can move the agreement to signature form.

Best,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of USD 400,000, payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices, less applicable withholdings and deductions. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the Company's employee benefit plans generally made available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to the terms and conditions of such plans, as amended from time to time. The Executive shall also be eligible to receive an annual discretionary target bonus equal to forty percent (40%) of the Executive's then-current annual base salary, based on achievement of Company and individual performance objectives established by the Company, as determined by the Board or its Compensation Committee in its discretion, and subject to the Executive's continued employment through the applicable payment date except as expressly provided in this Agreement. Any equity or equity-based participation shall be subject to approval by the Board or its Compensation Committee and shall be documented separately under the Company's applicable equity incentive plan and award agreements.
edits.name: Compensation counterproposal

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive's employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, then, subject to the Executive's execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims in favor of the Company and continued compliance with all restrictive covenants, the Executive shall receive: (a) severance equal to nine months of the Executive's then-current base salary, payable in substantially equal installments in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices; and (b) if the Executive timely elects continuation coverage under COBRA, reimbursement of the employer portion of COBRA premiums for the Executive and the Executive's covered dependents for up to nine months following the termination date, or, if earlier, until the Executive becomes eligible for group health coverage through another employer. For purposes of this Agreement, 'Good Reason' shall mean, without the Executive's written consent, a material diminution in the Executive's base salary, a material diminution in the Executive's authority, duties, or responsibilities, or the Company's material breach of this Agreement, provided that the Executive gives written notice within thirty days after the event, the Company has thirty days to cure, and the Executive resigns within thirty days after expiration of the cure period if the condition remains uncured.
edits.name: Enhanced severance and Good Reason

edits.text: 4. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS. During employment and for nine months following the termination of employment for any reason, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly: (a) solicit, induce, or encourage any employee, consultant, or independent contractor of the Company to terminate or reduce such relationship with the Company, or hire or engage any such person; or (b) solicit or knowingly interfere with any material customer, prospective customer, vendor, supplier, or business partner of the Company with whom the Executive had material contact or about whom the Executive obtained confidential information during employment, in each case for the purpose of providing products or services competitive with those of the Company. The Executive shall also remain bound by customary confidentiality, non-disclosure, invention assignment, intellectual property, and return-of-property obligations in favor of the Company, to be included in this Agreement or ancillary agreements. These covenants shall apply only to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, and nothing herein shall prohibit the Executive from engaging in lawful conduct that cannot be restricted under applicable law.
edits.name: Replace non-compete with tailored non-solicit/confidentiality/IP protections

receiver.message_back: Counsel, we can recommend proceeding if the signature draft reflects: (i) $425,000 base salary, 50% target bonus, and a stated initial equity grant to be approved at hire consistent with COO-level participation; (ii) 12 months’ base severance and COBRA on a without-Cause/Good-Reason termination; and (iii) the 9-month non-solicit limited to employees and customers with whom Executive had material business contact in the prior 12 months, excluding general solicitations and vendor/supplier restrictions. If Vireo can meet those points, please circulate the execution version and ancillary documents for final review.
